summary: Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig (Dr. phil. 1843), Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Burnouf, Bopp, and Wilson, among others. He was a long-time professor at the University of Oxford (1854, 1868–1900).

Friedrich Müller was an Austrian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Anton Boller at Vienna and earned his doctorate at Tübingen. He served as professor at the University of Vienna from 1869.

Friedrich Nietzsche worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the Universities of Bonn and Leipzig under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, earning his doctorate from Leipzig. From 1869 to 1878, he held a faculty post at the University of Basel.

Friedrich Otto Schrader was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Franz Kielhorn and Ernst Leumann at Göttingen and Strasbourg. He served as director of the Adyar Library (1905–1916) and later as professor at Kiel University (1921–1945).
Friedrich Ottomar Eduard Wilhelm held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1920–1924) and the University of Munich (~1924–1939).
Friedrich Ratzel studied at Heidelberg University (~1868–1869). He held academic posts at the Technical University of Munich (~1875–1886) and the University of Leipzig (~1886–1904).

Friedrich Rosen specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Leipzig (PhD), and under Franz Bopp and Henry Thomas Colebrooke. Rosen served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (~1828–1837).

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Jena (1810–1812) and studied under Franz Bopp and Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall. He served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826–1841) and Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Alexander Hamilton, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at the University of Jena (1800), University of Cologne (1804), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich Schleiermacher was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1789), where he later held a post (~1804–1807), before holding a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

Friedrich Schrader worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, earning his Ph.D. (~1887–1889), and worked as a librarian at the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1889–1891).

Friedrich Stamm, a scholar in linguistics and Indology, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Münster (~1914–1919). He held positions at the University and State Library of Münster and the Göttingen State and University Library (1921).

Friedrich Stolz worked in linguistics. He studied under Bernhard Jülg at Innsbruck, Georg Curtius at Leipzig, and earned his PhD at Graz (~1872–1874). He was later ordinary professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Innsbruck (1890–1912).
Friedrich Streiter was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1856 and earned his Ph.D. from Humboldt University of Berlin (1856–1861).

Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and August Conrady, earning his doctorate and Habilitation there. He later held Leipzig's chair of Indian philology from 1938 to 1958.

Friedrich Wilhelm was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Paul Thieme and earned his doctorate at the University of Munich (~1952–1956). He served as a professor at the University of Munich from 1969 to 1998.
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf worked in religious studies. He held posts at the University of Augsburg (~1992–1999) and the University of Munich (~1999–2014).

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at Tübingen and Leipzig. He was a professor at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1845).

Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under Sachau, Grube, and Gabelentz. He served as director of the East Asian department at Berlin's Ethnological Museum (1906–1928).

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl worked in linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Halle (Dr. phil. 1829), and held professorships at the University of Breslau (1834), University of Bonn (1839), and University of Leipzig (~1865–1875).
